short: Nazi Germany signed an unconditional surrender, ending the Second World War in Europe.
full:
On 8 May 1945, representatives of the German High Command signed the final instrument of unconditional surrender in Berlin, ceasing all military operations. Following the suicide of Adolf Hitler on 30 April and the rapid collapse of remaining German forces, an initial surrender had been signed on 7 May in Reims, France. However, the Soviet Union demanded a second, ratified signing ceremony in Berlin, which took effect late on 8 May.

The surrender marked the complete military and political collapse of the Third Reich and the end of the European theatre of the war. Millions celebrated Victory in Europe (V-E) Day across the Allied nations. Germany was subsequently divided into occupation zones administered by the United States, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom, and France, completely losing its sovereignty.
